taxon_or_scope: Cirsium comparative (C. vulgare + five native congeners)
design: paired bagged-vs-open heads plus pollen supplementation across populations
reproductive_assurance_context: autonomous selfing varies strongly among species
quantitative_anchor: C. vulgare had higher autonomous self-pollination than rare C. andrewsii and C. fontinale; 9/11 population pollen-limitation estimates were not different from zero
claim_boundary: one comparative data-generation study; species/populations are not independent studies and exact Fig. 6 values are not frozen

reproductive_assurance_context: animal pollination dependence despite adequate current pollination service
quantitative_anchor: supplement 41.75±11.39 n=8; control 47.88±9.44 n=8; bagged 12.2±3.57 n=5 seeds/flower; open/bagged RR=3.9246; bagged/open=0.2548; supplement/open=0.8720
claim_boundary: single meadow and small treatment n; open-vs-bagged indicates pollinator contribution, not pollen limitation

design: partial and complete pollinator exclusion with seed output and reproductive-failure outcome
reproductive_assurance_context: low autonomous assurance relative to invasive Carduus comparator
quantitative_anchor: 55% of complete-exclusion heads failed reproductively across the two thistles vs <7% in other treatments; any exclusion lowered seed output among heads with viable achenes; C. discolor lost more reproductive output than Carduus nutans
claim_boundary: 55% figure is pooled across two species and must not be treated as a C. discolor-specific effect size

reproductive_assurance_context: dioecy makes donor proximity a hard reproductive-assurance constraint
quantitative_anchor: female clones >=50 m from males set far fewer achenes; distance to nearest effective pollen donor negatively correlated with fertilization
claim_boundary: not a bagging experiment and no common lnRR can be combined with exclusion studies

design: bagged-vs-open capitula summarized in official recovery assessments
reproductive_assurance_context: self-fertile but autonomous selfing insufficient for high seed production
quantitative_anchor: bagging to prevent open pollination produced much lower seed set than non-bagged heads
claim_boundary: primary numerical table not yet recovered; keep sign-level until source data are obtained

design: reproductive biology field study in New Zealand
reproductive_assurance_context: cross-pollination depends on flowering synchrony and local density
quantitative_anchor: study concluded cross-pollination was required for fertile seed and that plants flowering in the main pollinator-active period or at sufficient density contributed most to the next generation
claim_boundary: contrasts with high autonomous selfing in the California comparative study; treat as evidence of context/population variability rather than a contradiction to average away
